maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 01 · SB 5.7.1–5 · Leadership by Following the Father

nodeData.topic: Session 01 · SB 5.7.1–5 · Leadership by Following the Father
nodeData.note: SB 5.7.1–5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Maharaj opens the series by showing that Bharata Maharaja's greatness came from rigidly following his father: he was chosen for sincerity and obedience, not by fame or voting, and that following empowered him to change the world. Perfect leadership means loving the citizens like one's own children and keeping everyone engaged; we lack such a king today because we lack the qualities to merit one. The animal sacrifices of old are forbidden in Kali-yuga, and sankirtana is the yajna for this age. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.topic: Following the father, step by step
children.note:
Bharata Maharaja was strict in religious principles because he walked fully in his father's footsteps. Maharaj draws out the point: Bharata is a follower who valued parampara.

🎙 Maharaj at 00:34 (auto-transcript): “That means that he is a follower and he valued parampara. Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow the instructions of our spiritual master in total.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 00:34

children.note:
Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how strictly we follow the instructions of our spiritual master, in total. — “Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow”

🎙 Maharaj at 00:52 (auto-transcript): “Our success in Krishna consciousness depends on how we rigidly follow the instructions of our spiritual master in total. So, Bharat Maharaj ruled a citizen very successfully.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 00:52

children.note: Maharaj asks why Bharata ruled the citizens so successfully, and answers: because he followed his father.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 01:36

children.note: Sukadeva Gosvami tells Pariksit how Bharata, by his father's order, began to rule the earth and married Pancajani.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 06:01

children.note:
Not by fame and not by scholarship. When the guru or the father sees sincerity and obedience, that person receives special attention. — “This is how to select a successor.”

🎙 Maharaj at 07:38 (auto-transcript): “This is how to select a successor. It's not by fame. It's not by scholarship. When the guru or the father sees the symptom of sincerity and obedience to the father or the guru, he will be given extra special attention.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 07:38

children.topic: No voting among a hundred sons
children.note:
Rishabhadeva had a hundred sons, yet there was no voting and no personal interest. It came naturally: Bharata manifested the qualities, so his father noticed him and placed him on the throne.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:46 (auto-transcript): “There was no voting here. Lord of Sabadev had warned on their songs. There were no voting. Among the hundreds, there were no voting. It came naturally. He manifested the qualities. Therefore, the father noticed him.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 09:46

children.note:
Maharaj sums it up as the natural sequence of empowerment, in one word: follow. — “Anyone who follows will be empowered.”

🎙 Maharaj at 11:26 (auto-transcript): “Anyone who follows will be empowered. This is a natural sequence of empowerment. Follow. Yes. Text number two. Just as a false ego creates the subtle sense objects, Maharaj Bharat created five sons in the womb of Panchajani, his wife. These sons were named Sumati, Rashtra…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 11:26

children.note: These verses name Bharata's five sons by Pancajani and tell how the land once called Ajanabha-varsa came to be known as Bharata-varsa.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 11:51

children.note:
No appointment, no campaign, no election — the world was changed simply by Bharata's purity. Maharaj asks what that potency is, and answers: following his father's footsteps. — “Everything is happening by the potency, the purity of Maharaj Bharat.”

🎙 Maharaj at 14:13 (auto-transcript): “Yes. Still no appointment. There is no appointment here. There is no campaign here. There is no election here. Everything is happening by the potency, the purity of Maharaj Bharat. It changed the world.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 14:13

children.note: This verse describes Bharata as an experienced ruler who cared for his citizens as his father and grandfather had, keeping them in their duties.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 15:34

children.note:
He was expert and learned because he received perfect training from his father; therefore he could rule perfectly.

🎙 Maharaj at 16:43 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj Bharat was experienced and well learned because he underwent perfect training from his father. Therefore, he perfectly ruled the citizens.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 16:43

children.note:
Maharaj puts the question to the room. Perfect rule means Bharata loved the citizens — he saw them exactly as he saw his own children.

🎙 Maharaj at 17:34 (auto-transcript): “What do we mean by perfect leadership, perfect rule? What is perfect rule? leadership. Perfect rule means Maharaj Bharat was as affectionate to the citizens as his father and grandfather had been. It means what? He loved the citizens.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 17:34

children.note:
Following Srila Prabhupada's purport, a chief executive must keep every citizen engaged in his occupational duty. That is perfect leadership.

🎙 Maharaj at 18:45 (auto-transcript): “And he kept all the citizens busy, engaged in their occupational duties. As Papa said, it is most important that a chief executive rules the citizens by keeping them fully engaged in their respective occupational duties. This is perfect leadership. Everyone was being engaged.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 18:45

children.note:
Out of love he maintained varnashrama: brahmanas, ksatriyas, vaisyas and sudras each engaged, and the spiritual orders of brahmacari, grihastha, vanaprastha and sannyasi visibly present.

🎙 Maharaj at 19:43 (auto-transcript): “Because Bharat Maharaj loved the citizens, he divided the citizens, he maintained the Varnashram system, he maintained Varnashram system. Brahmanas, Chatriyas, Vaishyas, Chudras were perfectly engaged.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 19:43

children.note:
If we want peace under our leadership, everyone must be engaged; no one should be left unemployed or unoccupied. — “No one should remain unemployed or unoccupied in any way.”

🎙 Maharaj at 21:30 (auto-transcript): “No one should remain unemployed or unoccupied in any way. This is leadership. That is, if we want the peace in our leadership, everyone must be engaged. Although formerly the government was a monarchy, all the kings were very affectionate towards the citizens and they…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 21:30

children.note:
Maharaj asks the audience his own question before taking theirs: why is there no Maharaja Bharata today?

🎙 Maharaj at 23:17 (auto-transcript): “We can see that we don't have Barat Mahdash now. Yes, it is true. We don't have Maharaj Bharat now. We don't have him now. Why? We don't have Maharaj Bharat. I know many questions are coming. Let me ask you my own question first before you start. Can you tell me, why there is…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 23:17

children.note:
Devotees answer: no disciplic succession followed, Kali-yuga, no varnashrama, no father like Rishabhadeva, no spiritual education from childhood, Krishna not at the centre, leaders seeking sense gratification, great people not wanting to lead.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:29 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna, Gurudev. Please accept my most humble of instances. Gurudev, I think because no disciplic succession was following that that is why Okay, very good, thank you because Kaliyuga Very good And Varnashram system was also missing that is also the reason Gurudev Very…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 24:29

children.topic: Citizens must merit such a king
children.note:
Maharaj's answer: to have a Bharata Maharaja there must also be good citizens who merit his qualities. We do not have him because we lack those qualities ourselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 28:16 (auto-transcript): “To have Barat Maharaj, to have Barat Maharaj, there should be also good citizens that will merit Barat Maharaj qualities. To have Barat Maharaj, today, we don't have him today because we also lack the qualities or merit, the quality of Bharat Maharaj. We shouldn't blame our…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 28:16

children.note:
We should not blame our leaders, because they are the combined consciousness of the people. — “our leaders, they are aggregate consciousness of the citizens.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:47 (auto-transcript): “We shouldn't blame our leaders because our leaders, they are aggregate consciousness of the citizens. If we are good children, we have good parents.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 28:47

children.note:
If we are good children we have good parents; the parents' consciousness produces the child, and the child's consciousness reflects the parents. Everything is connected.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:18 (auto-transcript): “If we are good children, we have good parents. The consciousness of the parent produces a child. The child's consciousness is also the result of the parent's consciousness. So we are all connected. Everything is connected.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 29:18

children.note:
We all contribute to what is happening today, so we are all responsible for it.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:06 (auto-transcript): “So we are all responsible for what is happening today. All of us are responsible. We contribute to what is happening. Toh is sab ke liye, ham sab log sayam jimmedar hain. Ham sayam is ke bhaagidar bhi hain. Take summa five. Paanchwa number shlok, agla. With great faith, King…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 30:06

children.note: This verse lists the many Vedic sacrifices Bharata performed with great faith, sometimes fully and sometimes in part, to worship the Supreme Lord.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 30:20

children.topic: Why such yajnas are forbidden now
children.note:
These sacrifices are not required today — they are forbidden. They were never meant for the participants to eat flesh; their purpose was to test the priests' ability and to give the offered animal a new, young body.

🎙 Maharaj at 31:42 (auto-transcript): “Now these Jagyas are not, they are not required, they are forbidden, yes, they are forbidden. Because these yagya were not performed for the performers or the participants to eat the flesh of the animals.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 31:42

children.note:
Because we have become fallen, there are no priests able to give the old animal a young body and achieve the result, so these yajnas have stopped.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:56 (auto-transcript): “Because we became fallen, therefore there is no qualified priest to perform this jagia that the old animal will be reunited to a young body and the perfect result is achieved because this preparation is no more there, therefore these jaggy eyes are being stopped. So prophets…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 33:56

children.note:
From the purport, Maharaj recites the verse quoted in Caitanya-caritamrta naming five things forbidden in this age, and explains that sankirtana-yajna, the congregational chanting of Hare Krishna, replaces the old sacrifices.

🎙 Maharaj at 34:40 (auto-transcript): “So prophets quoted in this Chitama Pundis Loka Aswamedam Gavalambham Sanyasam Fala Paitrikam Dibarena Support Patim Kalu Panchar Ibarajayet In this age of Kali Five acts are forbidden The offering of a horse and sacrifice is forbidden The offering of a cow in sacrifice is…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 34:40

children.note:
Of the old sacrifices, all are forbidden; the chanting of the holy name is the one that still works today.

🎙 Maharaj at 38:41 (auto-transcript): “So the five things which are forbidden, they are forbidden, only one is still functioning. The instructions refer not to Krishna devotees who are preaching Krishna Consciousness.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 38:41

children.note:
The ban on sannyasa does not apply to devotees who preach Krishna consciousness. It is meant for ordinary people who take sannyasa only to fill their belly without preaching. — “It is meant for ordinary people who take sanyas”

🎙 Maharaj at 39:13 (auto-transcript): “The instructions refer not to Krishna devotees who are preaching Krishna Consciousness. It is meant for ordinary people who take sanyas only to fold their belly without preaching.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 39:13

children.note:
Two questions from devotees; the rest were held over to the next day.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:44 (auto-transcript): “take the questions or any comments, the devotees can raise their hand and one by one they can ask the question answers. So, Disha Mataji, you can unmute and please ask your question. Hare Krishna Maharaj, please accept my humble obeisances. Maharaj, I got many questions today…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 41:44

children.topic: Q1 · Would Mother Durga want blood?
children.note:
If Durga or Kali is the mother of all living beings, how could she be pleased by the killing of her own children in bali?

🎙 Question from the floor at 42:01 (auto-transcript): “Hare Krishna Maharaj, please accept my humble obeisances. Maharaj, I got many questions today while listening to the class, but in that the most important which I felt Maharaj, Like Kali Devi or Durga Devi, she is a mother of all the living entities. Then why in the Shastras…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 42:01

children.note:
Durga does not want any animal killed for her and considers such worshippers foolish. She likes devotees more than her worshippers, so we please her best by worshipping Krishna. — “So it's better that we worship Krishna so we make her happy.”

🎙 Maharaj at 44:07 (auto-transcript): “Actually, Durga does not want a goat or any animal to be healed for her. She doesn't like it. Therefore, she considered her worshippers to be fully fools. She liked devotees than her worshippers. So it's better that we worship Krishna so we make her happy.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 44:07

children.topic: Q2 · How can partial sacrifices succeed?
children.note:
The purport says Bharata sometimes performed sacrifices partially. If anything but bhakti fails when left incomplete, how did partial sacrifices give results?

🎙 Question from the floor at 45:49 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, here in the purpose, Prabhupada mentioned that Bharat Maharaj, he was performing the sacrifices completely and partially also. So complete sacrifices understood but it's for 100 years and partially means he used to do it for 50 years something like that and if if…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 45:49

children.note:
Performing partially means he chose the most important, essential parts and did those rather than every detail — and because he selected the essence, he got the full result.

🎙 Maharaj at 46:58 (auto-transcript): “Hashi Ali means that he was selecting all the essential things and he would perform that, not all the full details. He would select all the few essence, most important things and do that. That is what he means by Hashi Ali. And because he selected already the most important…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 01 | SB 5.7.1–5 | BDDSwami | Dec 03, 2024 · 46:58

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 02 · SB 5.7.6–7 · Consciousness Makes the Difference

nodeData.topic: Session 02 · SB 5.7.6–7 · Consciousness Makes the Difference
nodeData.note: SB 5.7.6–7 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja performed Vedic sacrifices to many demigods, yet his heart was fixed on Vasudeva, seeing each demigod as a limb of the Lord. Maharaj teaches that consciousness makes the difference — illustrated by watering the root of a tree and by Nimbarkacarya, whose dutiful worship of Shiva led him to Radha and Krishna — and warns against criticising the acts of pure devotees. In the questions he explains being in the dham by consciousness, the two ways of seeing Krishna everywhere, and becoming pure amid one's duties. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 03 · SB 5.7.8–11 · From Throne to Pulaha-asrama
nodeData.note: SB 5.7.8–11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. After an immense reign Bharata Maharaja hands his kingdom to his sons in good order and leaves for Pulaha-asrama, where the Lord still appears to devotees in the form they love and the Gandaki purifies all it touches. Maharaj shows that Pulaha-asrama is higher than any kingdom, and that Bharata's simple worship with leaves, flowers, fruits and water is the only process that gives real peace. In a long question session he explains how to stay happy among devotees of different levels and why scriptures must be heard from sadhus. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: When his destined time of royal enjoyment ended, Bharata divided his inherited wealth among his sons and left home for Pulaha-asrama, where salagrama-silas are found.

nodeData.topic: Session 04 · SB 5.7.12–14 · The Heart Melts in Love
nodeData.note: SB 5.7.12–14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Constant absorption in devotional service brings results: Bharata Maharaja's heart melts, ecstatic symptoms appear on his body, and he rises beyond regulative practice to the bhava stage. Maharaj contrasts this with our fluctuation, explains that bhakti shows in one's life as Pundarika Vidyanidhi saw in Gadadhara Pandita, and describes Bharata's worship of Narayana within the sun — the Lord who is both greater and smaller than everything. Questions cover Gayatri and the maha-mantra, steady practice, deerskin, aham brahmasmi and the meaning of bhakti. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 05 · SB 5.8.1–5 · The Lion's Roar and the Doe

nodeData.topic: Session 05 · SB 5.8.1–5 · The Lion's Roar and the Doe
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.1–5 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Chapter 8 opens the great lesson of Bharata Maharaja's life — misplaced affection, misunderstood compassion and the power of association. As Bharata chants by the Gandaki, a pregnant doe comes to drink, a lion roars, and in fear she leaps and her fawn falls into the river; Maharaj teaches that renunciation is in the heart, that Maya is always present, and that the loud noise of sense gratification drowns out the holy name. A network failure cut the class short, and the questions cover fear in bhakti, protecting pregnant women, Astavakra Muni and how to tune down the mind. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 06 · SB 5.8.6–9 · The Fawn and Excess Compassion

nodeData.topic: Session 06 · SB 5.8.6–9 · The Fawn and Excess Compassion
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.6–9 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The orphaned fawn enters Bharata Maharaja's life, and Maharaj calls this the beginning of the problem: real compassion raises a soul to Krishna consciousness, while compassion for bodily comfort becomes attachment. He holds the episode up as a mirror for devotees whose japa starves while they chase position, and answers questions on attachment, karma and keeping sixteen rounds amid service. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse tells how the pregnant doe, separated from her flock and exhausted by her leap across the river, collapses in a cave and dies. Maharaj notes how delicate a pregnant mother's condition is, and that she leapt out of fear of the lion.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 06 | SB 5.8.6–9 | BDDSwami | Dec 10, 2024 · 13:32

children.note: Bharata Maharaja sees the newborn fawn floating in the river, feels compassion and carries it to his asrama. Maharaj says: this is the beginning of the problem.

children.topic: Everyone in this world is sleeping
children.note:

nodeData.topic: Session 07 · SB 5.8.10–13 · Bound to the Deer
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.10–13 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja reasons that he must protect the fawn, then eats, sleeps, walks and plays with it until his heart is bound. Maharaj applies the lesson bluntly to devotees who keep cats and dogs out of frustration, and to those who rush back to what they once rejected as maya; in a long Q&A he speaks on Kali-yuga, steadiness, Rupa Kaviraja's offence, tolerance and Ekadasi. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The verse gives Bharata Maharaja's reasoning that an advanced person feels for the suffering and should protect one who has surrendered, even at personal cost. Maharaj reads the purport's warning against welfare work done only in bodily terms.

nodeData.topic: Session 08 · SB 5.8.14–21 · Misplaced Affection
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.14–21 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja breaks off his worship to check on the deer, and when it wanders away he laments like a miser who has lost his wealth. Maharaj calls this misplaced affection and asks what our lives would be like if this same absorption were turned to Krishna, praying like Rupa Gosvami and Queen Kunti. Questions cover family attachment, distractions in japa, marriage, judging others, and pets. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 09 · SB 5.8.22–25 · Blind Love
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.22–25 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja, speaking like a madman, praises the deer's footprints, talks to the moon and burns with the fever of separation from his 'son'. Maharaj calls it blind love, warns that we can leave the track of pure bhakti while seeming to be on it, and explains from the purport why Krishna gave Bharata a deer's body — to intensify his desire for devotional service. Questions cover a dying puppy, heaven, loyalty to guru, initiation, and attachment in preaching. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Bharata Maharaja remembers fondly how the deer would bite the kusa grass laid out for sacrifice, and sit still like a sage's son when pushed away. Polluting what was meant for Krishna was nothing to him.

Just like when the children contaminate the items to be worshipped to the Lord or the items to be used in the service of Krishna, some parents, they feel, no, it's okay. So exactly the Buddha…”

nodeData.topic: Session 10 · SB 5.8.26–31 · Death, Deer Birth, Repentance
nodeData.note: SB 5.8.26–31 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja dies seeing the deer at his side and takes a deer's body, but by Krishna's grace remembers his past life and repents constantly. Maharaj ties this to the quality of our sadhana, the need not to waste a moment, and the danger of fallen devotees comforting each other; the deer leaves its mother and lives quietly at Pulaha-asrama. Questions range over the mind, Ekadasi, strong sadhana, offences in the dham and true repentance. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: At death Bharata Maharaja sees the deer sitting by him like a grieving son; his mind absorbed in it, he takes the body of a deer — yet he does not forget his past life.

nodeData.topic: Session 11 · SB 5.9.1–3 · Born again, never falling twice
nodeData.note: SB 5.9.1–3 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Bharata Maharaja takes birth in a highly qualified brahmana family, showing Krishna's promise that no sincere effort in devotion is lost. Remembering his one mistake, he never repeats it: he appears dull, deaf and mad so that no one disturbs him, and stays absorbed in the Lord within. Maharaj urges everyone to plan their own Krishna consciousness so that nothing can break in. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 12 · SB 5.9.4–8 · The son who would not learn
nodeData.note: SB 5.9.4–8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Jada Bharata's father lovingly tries to train him in brahminical rules, but the son, finished with material duties, plays the fool and keeps only to pure devotion. Maharaj uses this to show determination, the mirror of Krishna consciousness and the point of no compromise; the father dies still attached, and the brothers give up on him, which only frees him for bhakti. Questions cover practising before preaching, a self-realised father's attachment, and how to stop forgetting the goal. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 13 · SB 5.9.9–14 · Mistreated, satisfied, surrendered
nodeData.note: SB 5.9.9–14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Treated as a fool by his stepfamily, Jada Bharata eats whatever comes, works their fields for scraps and is untouched by insult, until dacoits seize him as a sacrifice for Bhadrakali and he still does not protest. Maharaj contrasts the world's idea of usefulness with the work of a paramahamsa, who changes hearts, and holds up Jada Bharata as full surrender. The questions cover his strength, tolerance in practice, being scolded unfairly and the lamentation of the acaryas. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 14 · SB 5.9.15–20 · Fearless before Kali's sword

nodeData.topic: Session 14 · SB 5.9.15–20 · Fearless before Kali's sword
nodeData.note: SB 5.9.15–20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. The dacoits decorate Jada Bharata, seat him before Kali and raise the sword, and he stays perfectly calm, knowing nothing happens without the Lord's sanction. Goddess Kali bursts from the deity and destroys the offenders, showing how the Lord protects devotees who know they are not the body. In the questions Maharaj contrasts Arjuna's acted bewilderment, false and realised fearlessness, and love that grows from attentive hearing. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
Maharaj praises a devotee's recitation of Queen Kunti's prayers. The host recalls Maharaj's teaching from the Nectar of Instruction, that one approaches a gosvami to become one, and welcomes him to narrate Jada Bharata's character.

🎙 Maharaj at 10:20 (auto-transcript): “This is great Wonderful thank you so much very very good thank you thank you very much Anirag Prabhu for inspiring all of us and tomorrow we will have Romil Mataji from Gurdagam and next Tuesday we will have Abhishek Kesarwani Prabhu from Chitra Koot so you all can be ready…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 10:20

children.note: The dacoits bathe, dress, decorate and feed Jada Bharata, then seat him before Kali with incense, lamps, music and prayers, as their own ritual for killing a man-animal requires.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 20:12

children.note:
This verse, Maharaj says, shows the supreme character of Jada Bharata. He behaved deaf, dumb and dull as an outer cover he designed for himself; within he was a paramahamsa. — “His intelligence was not dull.”

🎙 Maharaj at 22:49 (auto-transcript): “This actually showed the supreme karat of Jal Bharat Exactly the verse said The supreme karat of Jal Bharat This verse showed the supreme karat of Jal Bharat Although he behaved like deaf, dumb, dull,”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 22:49

children.note:
He knew perfectly well they were taking him to be killed for Kali, and still he was never afraid. Maharaj exclaims at what a supreme character he is.

🎙 Maharaj at 24:11 (auto-transcript): “So Jhad Bhara was aware that they were taking him to be killed, the sacrifice for Godess Kali. What a supreme character he is.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 24:11

children.topic: A pure devotee is never disturbed
children.note: Maharaj turns to Srila Prabhupada's description of a pure devotee in Bhagavad-gita chapter 12: such a devotee sees difficulty as the Lord's mercy and stays calm, quiet and patient, exactly like Jada Bharata.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 25:23

children.note:
He ate everything they offered him. Maharaj asks who could eat with death in front of him; Jada Bharata was peaceful and normal, while we become completely disorganised when any disturbing situation comes. — “When death is before somebody, who will have time to eat?”

🎙 Maharaj at 31:15 (auto-transcript): “He ate everything they offered him, he ate everything. When death is before somebody, who will have time to eat? The feeling cannot align the truth of anything, but it's peaceful, it's normal, no anxiety.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 31:15

children.note:
He knows his Lord is right there. If something happens, the Lord has sanctioned it, and neither Indra, Brahma nor Shiva can change it; if anyone did, it would only interfere with our Krishna consciousness. With this realisation a devotee stays calm in every situation. — “If something happens, that means the Lord sanction it.”

🎙 Maharaj at 32:51 (auto-transcript): “Why? He knows my Lord is just before me here. So, what can happen? My Lord is here. If something happens, that means the Lord sanction it. Otherwise, it will not happen. And if the law is sanctioned, who can change it? And if the law is sanctioned, who can change it?”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 32:51

children.note: One of the thieves, acting as priest, consecrates a fearsome sword with Bhadrakali's mantra and raises it to kill Jada Bharata and offer his blood to the goddess.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 34:49

children.note:
Even then he was peaceful. Maharaj says we are learning the depth of Jada Bharata's conviction about Krishna: he saw everything and was not afraid. — “When situation does not change our faith in Krishna, that is transcendence.”

🎙 Maharaj at 36:00 (auto-transcript): “Still, he was peaceful. We are learning the level of conviction for Jabara's Krishna consciousness. How much is convinced about Krishna?”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 36:00

children.note:
A godbrother recently asked Maharaj why Krishna allowed devotees to be killed in Bangladesh instead of coming and destroying the attackers. Maharaj answers: let us see what Krishna did here.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:46 (auto-transcript): “A few days ago, one god-brother asked me, Why? Why? Krishna allowed devotees to be killed in Bangladesh. Krishna should have just come and top up their head and killed all of them. Why Krishna didn't? Well, let's see what Krishna did.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 39:46

children.note: The dacoits, low-minded, bound by passion and ignorance and greedy for wealth, defy the Vedic injunctions so far as to prepare to kill a brahmana-born soul.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 40:44

children.note:
Killing a brahmana brings suffering on generations of one's family. Jada Bharata is more than a brahmana: a Vaishnava fully absorbed in Krishna and the friend of all living beings. Nothing is more dangerous than this, and there was no reason at all to kill him. — “It is very dangerous to kill a Brahmana.”

🎙 Maharaj at 41:55 (auto-transcript): “It is very dangerous to kill a Brahmana. Generations of one's family members who will suffer for this offense. is”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 41:55

children.note: Unable to tolerate the offence to a great devotee, Goddess Kali bursts out of the deity in an unbearable effulgence.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 46:01

children.topic: The offenders meet their own sword
children.note: In fury Kali leaps from the altar, beheads the dacoits with the very sword meant for Jada Bharata, and she and her associates revel in their blood.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 49:02

children.note:
Maharaj points out the reversal: an offence to a superior devotee takes away one's life and opulence. They wanted to offer Jada Bharata's blood to Kali; instead Kali drank theirs.

🎙 Maharaj at 51:48 (auto-transcript): “When we will find a superior devotee, the duration of our life and all opulences are taken away. He wants to offer Jadbaradi blood to Gaudi Kali, but Gaudi Kali drunk their own blood.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 51:48

children.note:
Maharaj reads the purport on why worshippers who offer abominable things to Kali for material gain are not protected by her.

🎙 Maharaj at 52:49 (auto-transcript): “It is evident, this is Prabhupada speaking, it is evident from this verse that the devotees of Goddess Kali are not at all favoured by her. It is Goddess Kali's work to kill and punish the demons. Goddess Kali, Durga, engages in decapitating many demons, darkoids, and other…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 52:49

children.note: Sukadeva Gosvami concludes that those who know the soul is distinct from the body and wish no one harm are always protected by the Lord, so such an escape is not at all surprising.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 55:34

children.note:
Maharaj reads the purport's summary of a pure devotee: fixed in his spiritual identity, therefore fearless, not treating even an enemy as an enemy, and fully dependent on the Lord's protection. This closes chapter 9.

🎙 Maharaj at 57:36 (auto-transcript): “Papa says, These are some of the great qualities of a pure devotee of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. First, a devotee is firmly convinced of his spiritual identity. He never identifies with the body.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 57:36

children.note:
Devotees ask about Arjuna's agitation, love for family over Krishna, fearless non-devotees, how much of Jada Bharata to follow, and loving a Krishna we cannot see.

🎙 Maharaj at 60:16 (auto-transcript): “Dear devotees, if you have any question or comment, we can raise our hands. Arjun Prabhu Ji, you can unmute and ask your question. Hare Krishna Guru Maharaj Danvat Pranam please accept my respectful and humble opinion to you Maharaj as you just mentioned the great qualities…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 60:16

children.note:
Jada Bharata stayed calm facing death, yet Arjuna, with Krishna right in front of him, was agitated. How to understand this?

🎙 Question from the floor at 60:41 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj as you just mentioned the great qualities of a pure devotee like as we just heard that Bharat Maharaj was not even agitated in the face of death but Maharaj in Mahabharat we have seen that even Arjun was a very dear friend and great devotee of Sri Krishna and Sri…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 60:41

children.note:
Arjuna is acting the part of a conditioned soul so that Krishna can give the Bhagavad-gita to us through him; otherwise how would Krishna speak to us? It is a drama for our benefit. — “Jad Bharat is not acting, he is living his straight life.”

🎙 Maharaj at 62:02 (auto-transcript): “Arjuna is acting as a conditional soul. So that Krishna can pass on Bhagavad Gita to us, through him, as a condition so.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 62:02

children.topic: Q2 · Why love family, not Krishna?
children.note:
A devotee asks why affection for husband, wife or children comes so naturally, but not for Krishna, though we know He is great.

🎙 Question from the floor at 64:26 (auto-transcript): “we are sometimes so much attached naturally to somebody our affection for somebody is so natural they may not be very great like maybe our lover our children uh our husband wife but why this attachment and affection is not towards krishna even after knowing that he is so…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 64:26

children.note:
We have material attachment to family, so we worry when something happens to them. We do not yet love Krishna, so the feeling is not there. Once love comes it is the same; look at the gopis.

🎙 Maharaj at 65:40 (auto-transcript): “We have material attachment for, we have material section for our husbands, our wives and family members and friends. therefore when something happens we are worried we don't have love for Krishna therefore there's no feelings that attachment is not there because we don't…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 65:40

children.note:
Maharaj tells of the brahmanas' wives: their husbands heard the cowherd boys' request and felt nothing, but the wives fainted on hearing that Krishna was hungry. Krishna had told the boys not to say it, knowing the wives' devotion; when they did, the wives rose and carried all the food in the house to Him themselves.

🎙 Maharaj at 66:22 (auto-transcript): “The moment the wise or the Brahman has heard that Krisha is hungry, they fainted, they They were unconscious. Why? They have love for Krishna.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 66:22

children.note:
Krishna prepared Himself to receive them, standing with one foot crossed over the other, a flower at His ear, twirling a leaf. Being married, they did not embrace Him physically, but their souls entered Him, and both were fully satisfied. — “The difference is question of love.”

🎙 Maharaj at 70:15 (auto-transcript): “And when we were getting closer to where Krishna was standing, Krishna prepared himself. Put the right foot over the left foot. He put a karnika flower here.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 70:15

children.note:
A devotee asks how some non-devotees who work for society's welfare are also unafraid of death.

🎙 Question from the floor at 72:37 (auto-transcript): “devotees have Krishna so they don't fear but sometimes we see good people living for welfare of societies they also don't fear even they are non-devotee how they don't fear of death Even when they are not devotee of Krishna. So, Mataji ka prishna hai ki aap ne yaa par bataya…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 72:37

children.note:
Their fearlessness stands on false ground: they lock their doors, keep dogs, and eat, sleep, mate and defend out of fear. A pure devotee's fearlessness is realised, not book knowledge, like Prahlada Maharaja, who saw the Lord face to face. — “Their fearlessness is on a false ground.”

🎙 Maharaj at 73:21 (auto-transcript): “Their fearlessness is on a false ground. They don't lock their doors. Dogs. Door. Door. Door. Door. Dog. Dog. Locking doors means what?”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 73:21

children.topic: Q4 · Must we be so extreme?
children.note:
Jada Bharata's renunciation is extreme. Must we live like that to attain Krishna, and what should we practically take from him?

🎙 Question from the floor at 77:31 (auto-transcript): “Shila Gurudev, Meena Mataji's question is that in this chapter, we are seeing extreme denunciation of Jadh Bharat. He is not eating, he is not sleeping, everything about him is very extreme, supreme. So what we are supposed to learn from Jalabharadji and apply in our life,…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 77:31

children.note:
We cannot do everything he did, but some things we can and must: firm conviction in Krishna, readiness to sacrifice anything that does not support our Krishna consciousness, blocking out distractions, and molding our life, as Srila Prabhupada asked, so that we remain Krishna conscious. — “You can have a firm conviction in Krishna.”

🎙 Maharaj at 78:17 (auto-transcript): “Few days ago, I mentioned in the class, this very class, that the things that Bharat is doing, we cannot do all that. Yes, it is a thing we can do, but there are some things we can do, which we need to do.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 78:17

children.note:
The gopis could see and talk with Krishna; we love those we can see. How can we love Krishna more when we cannot see Him?

🎙 Question from the floor at 86:41 (auto-transcript): “Thank you. First of all, sorry, I am like a child. I ask stupid questions. So, I apologize. And second, like you explain when Mataji right now how gopi is love for the Krishna so gopi's love for the Krishna is instantaneous as what I know I don't know what is correct gopis…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 86:41

children.note:
Rukmini never saw Krishna; she only heard about Him and developed love. Krishna says in the Gita that some reach the goal simply by hearing from authorities. Our only problem is that we do not hear. — “Therefore, hearing is very, very important.”

🎙 Maharaj at 88:54 (auto-transcript): “Rukmani Devi did not see Krishna. She only heard about Krishna. She didn't see, only hearing. So, if you don't see physically, who can see through the ear? Therefore, hearing is very, very important.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 88:54

children.note:
Arjuna heard 700 verses in about thirty minutes, and Pariksit Maharaja heard the Bhagavatam for seven days and said Krishna had been planted in his heart. In Gita 18.72–73 Krishna asks whether Arjuna heard attentively, and the proof is that his illusion is gone. The difference is the quality of hearing.

🎙 Maharaj at 91:09 (auto-transcript): “Arjun had Bhagavad Gita for 30 minutes 30 minutes not one hour 30 minutes we have difficulty memorizing one verse but Arjun goes 700 verses in 30 minutes 700 he was not a Brahmana he's a Satriya the problem is the quality of hearing Parishit Maharaj had”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 14 | SB 5.9.15–20 | BDDSwami | Dec 27, 2024 · 91:09

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 15 · SB 5.10.1–6 · Carrying the king's palanquin

nodeData.topic: Session 15 · SB 5.10.1–6 · Carrying the king's palanquin
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.1–6 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Chapter 10 opens with King Rahugana's servants forcing Jada Bharata to carry the palanquin. He walks carefully to avoid stepping on ants, which Maharaj reads as preparation to show the king compassion, and he takes the king's sarcasm in silence because he knows he is not the body. Maharaj also explains why one should not cut short any creature's allotted life, and answers questions on mosquitoes, becoming a paramahamsa and abortion. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note:
After a devotee recites Queen Kunti's prayers, Maharaj joins the class from outdoors. Asked if he is ready, he answers that Bhagavatam is everywhere and he is always ready. Chapter 10, the discussion between Jada Bharata and King Rahugana, begins.

🎙 Maharaj at 09:34 (auto-transcript): “Yes, we are somewhere. And everywhere is. Everywhere, Bhagavatam. Everywhere. Okay. We are always ready. We are always ready. Thank you. Thank you so much Shila Gurudev. So we are extremely grateful to Shila Gurudev, although he is outside, but Shila Gurudev is ready for us…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 09:34

children.note:
Maharaj frames the first eight texts: they show Jada Bharata's humility and compassion, and King Rahugana's judgements of him. He asks everyone to listen carefully for the messages Jada Bharata is teaching.

🎙 Maharaj at 21:25 (auto-transcript): “So in this chapter, from text 1 to 8, we will see Jad Bharat, humility and compassion. And they will see Rahugana's assessments of Next, number one.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 21:25

children.note: On the way to Kapila's asrama, King Rahugana's carriers need one more man at the Iksumati river; seeing Jada Bharata young and strong, they press him into carrying the palanquin.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 22:06

children.note:
Maharaj says the chapter shows Jada Bharata's successive challenges in Krishna consciousness and his full faith in Krishna, humility and compassion.

🎙 Maharaj at 25:17 (auto-transcript): “What we are seeing is Jad Bharat's successive challenges in his Krishna consciousness Yes. And the demonstration of his full condition in Krishna, his faith in Krishna, his humility and his compassion.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 25:17

children.note:
Leaving his kingdom, falling into a deer's body, mistreatment by his stepfamily, the Kali worshippers, now the palanquin and soon the king's rebuke: through all of it his Krishna consciousness remains. — “His Krishna consciousness is remaining.”

🎙 Maharaj at 27:14 (auto-transcript): “when he left his kingdom or the forest he had difficulties. Because Krishna consciousness remained. He fell down and became a dear. His Krishna consciousness remained.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 27:14

children.note:
According to Sanatana Gosvami, Jada Bharata is a jnani-bhakta, a pure devotee with knowledge, while Arjuna is a premi-bhakta, an eternal associate of Krishna. There is a difference.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:08 (auto-transcript): “According to Sanatana Goswami, Jadbharad is a jnani bhakta. He's a pure devotee. He has knowledge. Arjuna is a premi bhakti. So there's difference. They are a tenor associative of Krishna. So here, the servant of Maharaj Rahugana, they are forcing him to carry the palanquin…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 15 | SB 5.10.1–6 | BDDSwami | Dec 28, 2024 · 30:08

children.note:

nodeData.topic: Session 16 · SB 5.10.7–11 · I am not the body
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.7–11 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Rahugana threatens Jada Bharata in anger, and Jada Bharata, untouched by the bodily conception, smiles and begins his reply: every insult was aimed at the body, not at the soul. Maharaj contrasts the king's passion with Srila Prabhupada's patience, shows how a pure devotee feels an insult only for a moment, and warns that worldly positions turn upside down. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 17 · SB 5.10.12–14 · Master, servant and the madman

nodeData.topic: Session 17 · SB 5.10.12–14 · Master, servant and the madman
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.12–14 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Jada Bharata tells Rahugana that master and servant are temporary labels under material nature, and that punishing someone he calls mad will achieve nothing — words that begin to turn the king's heart. Jada Bharata humbly takes up the palanquin again, and Maharaj draws from it, and from SB 10.14.8, that success in Krishna consciousness depends on a positive attitude that sees difficulties as Krishna's mercy. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The class takes up Canto 5, chapter 10 from text 12, as Jada Bharata goes on answering King Rahugana's sarcastic words.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 25:23

children.note:
Devotees have begun Bhismadeva's prayers after Kunti's. Maharaj asks them not to rush on and forget, but to absorb and feel each prayer before going to the next. — “let us digest it”

🎙 Maharaj at 02:08 (auto-transcript): “I think we should digest the properly let us digest it properly yes yeah we don't run to bisman and forget let us digest it okay let us let us absorb there and feel it then you remain water then we can go next okay we will do that So we will try that everyone digest it, and…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 02:08

children.note:
Vardhini Mataji apologises in advance for forgetting lines of Kunti's prayers. Maharaj reassures her not to worry and simply be herself. — “Just be yourself.”

🎙 Maharaj at 03:09 (auto-transcript): “Maharaj, please forgive me. I may forget some prayers. I've tried, but I may forget. Don't worry. Don't worry. Just be yourself. Don't do yourself. Don't worry. Just be yourself. Thank you, my God. Thank you. Satsang with Mooji”

children.note: Jada Bharata tells the king that the distinction of master and servant is temporary and that everyone is pushed by material nature; still, if the king wants to be master, he will obey.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 27:09

children.note:
Maharaj voices Jada Bharata: from your speech I can see you know nothing about the soul. On the bodily platform you claim to be master — fine, tell me what you want me to do. — “you have no knowledge about the self. Zero.”

🎙 Maharaj at 28:33 (auto-transcript): “In other words, Jad Bharat is saying, from your speech, I can understand that if I judge on the body, you have no knowledge about the self. Zero. That is your position. On the bodily platform, so you are claiming to be a master, I am the servant, so order me as a servant and…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 28:33

children.note:
The purport recalls Bhaktivinoda Thakura's image: men and women float like straws on the waves of material nature until they understand they are Krishna's eternal servants.

🎙 Maharaj at 29:46 (auto-transcript): “The Prophet said, Shila Bhaktivinathakura said that all men and women are floating like straws on the waves of material nature. If they come to their understanding that they are the eternal servant of Krishna, they will put an end to this floating condition. We have mentioned…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 29:46

children.topic: Serving the senses since time immemorial
children.note:
Maharaj says we never really act for ourselves, the soul; we do what the senses have dictated since time immemorial. Human life begins when we refuse their orders and act as the soul directs, as a devotee of Krishna.

🎙 Maharaj at 30:56 (auto-transcript): “We will never do something for ourselves. We will only do the things our senses have been detecting for us since time immemorial. Human life begins only when one becomes a devotee of Krishna.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 30:56

children.topic: All our desires belong to the body
children.note: Taking Bhagavad-gita 3.37, Maharaj asks who desires so many things under passion. It is the body and senses, not the soul, and we have foolishly followed; nature supplies those things and we become more entangled. — “None of it is the soul.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 32:26

children.note:
We play master or servant like actors directed by someone else; the real director is material nature. In human life we should end this stage show by agreeing to be controlled by Krishna and His servant.

🎙 Maharaj at 33:59 (auto-transcript): “For some time, we play as master or celebrant, as actor play on the stage under someone else's direction. While we are in the human form, we should put an end to this nonsensical stage performance. That is when the soul is not directing. At the present moment,”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 33:59

children.note: Jada Bharata answers the king's insults and threat: he only appears dull, he is self-realised; and if he really were mad, punishment would be wasted on him.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 36:36

children.note:
Maharaj restates the king's words — rascal, crazy fellow — and asks whether beating a madman will ever cure him.

🎙 Maharaj at 39:03 (auto-transcript): “You said I'm a rascal, I'm a doctor. I am a crazy fellow. So, can you courage a foolish person by beating? If he beat a madman, he will become cured.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 39:03

children.note:
What will the king gain by punishing a dead body or a mad person? It is like beating a horse that is already dead. — “Will you kill a dead horse?”

children.note:
The purport says everyone here works like a madman: a thief knows punishment follows, yet steals again, obsessed with the idea that stealing will make him happy. So punishment alone is useless.

🎙 Maharaj at 41:22 (auto-transcript): “So Prabha said, Everyone in this material world is working like a mad, under certain impressions, falsely acquired in a material condition for example a thief who knows that stealing is not good and who knows that it is followed by punishment by a king or by god who has seen…”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 41:22

children.note:
During Nigeria's military regime, Maharaj recalls, robbers were executed publicly at the beach as a warning. Thousands drove there to watch — and came back to find their own cars or tyres stolen. — “by the time they come back their own car have been stolen”

🎙 Maharaj at 43:03 (auto-transcript): “I remember during the military regime here in Nigeria, they will take Kibana people to the beach and kill them. So thousands of people used to go and watch the team being killed.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 43:03

children.note:
So Jada Bharata tells Rahugana that his punishment will not change him; the king does not understand what is happening and speaks like a fool. — “Your measure you are describing for punishment will not change me.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 46:00

children.note: Sukadeva tells Pariksit how Jada Bharata, peaceful and humble, tolerates the harsh words, replies properly, and goes back to carrying the palanquin, accepting it as the result of past karma.

The purport describes the devotee who sees reverses as the Lord's concession, is never angry with his master, and keeps on with his service — such a person is assured of going back to Godhead.

children.topic: The heir who simply stays alive
children.note:
Sridhara Svami's commentary: as a rightful son need only remain alive to inherit, one who simply remains in Krishna consciousness, following the principles of bhakti, becomes eligible for the Lord's mercy.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 60:46

children.note:
Remaining requires patience and tolerance. If we stay while grudging, complaining, worried or angry, the verse will not bear fruit; staying joyfully, accepting everything favourably, gives it meaning. — “That requires patience, tolerance.”

🎙 Maharaj at 62:00 (auto-transcript): “We should remain in Krishna consciousness. That requires patience, tolerance.”

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 17 | SB 5.10.12–14 | BDDSwami | Jan 02, 2025 · 62:00

Questions from devotees after the class.

Romil Mataji first thinks a difficulty is Krishna's plan, yet is still disturbed for a day or two before accepting it. Why?

Accepting that Krishna arranged it for our purification, the mind is still disturbed — that is normal while we have a body. Ignore it, go for the essence, and do not interfere with Krishna's plan.

Human nature will reflect, but when we use the higher self to control the lower self we succeed. — “the higher self to control the lower self”

Karma or test, both come to us through the guru for our good, and we should follow them all.

nodeData.topic: Session 18 · SB 5.10.15–17 · The king falls at his feet
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.15–17 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Because Rahugana has faith, Jada Bharata's words loosen the knot in his heart; he steps down from the palanquin, falls at the sage's feet and begs forgiveness, then asks who he is and confesses that he fears nothing so much as offending a brahmana. Maharaj teaches how to beg forgiveness sincerely, why accepting a guru is compulsory but must be done with care, and why an offence to a brahmana or Vaishnava reaches even the soul. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 19 · SB 5.10.18–20 · Seeking the secure shelter

nodeData.topic: Session 19 · SB 5.10.18–20 · Seeking the secure shelter
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.18–20 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Rahugana recognises the hidden greatness of Jada Bharata, asks him to explain his weighty words, accepts him as a representative of Kapila, and asks what the most secure shelter is and how he can advance. Maharaj shows that a bona fide guru needs a bona fide, attentive hearer, that accepting a guru is compulsory, and that only the question of how to advance spiritually takes us out of our situation. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: After a long gap the class resumes Canto 5, chapter 10, in the section where King Rahugana expresses humility and submission, beginning from text 18.

nodeData.topic: Session 20 · SB 5.10.21–25 · Rahugana Begs Forgiveness
nodeData.note: SB 5.10.21–25 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. King Rahugana argues that the soul really does feel the body's fatigue, pain and duties, and Maharaj answers with dreams, a clay pot, yogis in fire and a man grieving over his car: it is misidentification with the body that makes us suffer. Then the king falls at Jada Bharata's feet for forgiveness, and Maharaj stresses how dangerous an offence to a Vaishnava is, before answering questions on attachment, being cheated, and longing for a Giriraja sila. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

nodeData.topic: Session 21 · SB 5.11.1–3 · Vedavada and Tattvavada
nodeData.note: SB 5.11.1–3 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Chapter 11 opens with Jada Bharata telling King Rahugana that he talks like an expert without real experience, and Maharaj explains why the ignorant should first listen to realised souls. He then contrasts the Vedavadi, attached to the Vedas' promises of material elevation, with the tattvavadi who studies Bhagavad-gita and Srimad-Bhagavatam and sees Vasudeva in everything, and shows how all material happiness is like a dream. A long question session covers life's tests, worship of the Bhagavatam, dreams, fear, and accepting correction. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: The new chapter, texts 1 to 17, is entirely Jada Bharata answering, instructing and chastising King Rahugana.

maps.title: Bharata Maharaja · Session 22 · SB 5.11.4–8 · The Mind Binds and Frees

nodeData.topic: Session 22 · SB 5.11.4–8 · The Mind Binds and Frees
nodeData.note: SB 5.11.4–8 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Jada Bharata explains that the mind, coloured by the three modes, drives the senses into pious and impious work and carries the soul from body to body. Maharaj illustrates this with a new phone, a feverish patient who runs from a fire, and upside-down yogis who still get angry, and concludes that the mind is controlled only by fixing it on Krishna's lotus feet under the guidance of a pure devotee. A long question session covers practice and detachment, what lies beyond piety, guidance in a large society, and how to treat imperfect authorities. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Maharaj introduces the next five verses: Jada Bharata is teaching that our own mind is the cause of our entanglement in this world.

orbit.ref: The Exalted Character of Bharata Maharaja | Session 22 | SB 5.11.4–8 | BDDSwami | Jan 17, 2025 · 21:00

children.note: Bound by the three modes, the mind pushes the person through the senses into pious and impious activity, like an uncontrolled elephant, and so keeps him enjoying and suffering here.

nodeData.topic: Session 23 · SB 5.11.9–17 · Neglect the Mind
nodeData.note: SB 5.11.9–17 · a class by HH Bhakti Dhira Damodara Swami. Jada Bharata lists the mind's eleven functions and shows how, under the Lord's direction, they multiply into countless material activities that keep the soul wandering. Maharaj tells Srila Prabhupada's story of the 'liquid beauty' to show that we are attracted by illusion, explains the sleeping and the awakened soul, and ends the chapter with the instruction to conquer the mind by serving guru and Krishna — Prabhupada's one-word method: neglect the mind. Questions cover how to miss Krishna, the order of purification, and how to live in goodness by rising before four. Notes are our own summary of the class; tap a bubble's link to hear that moment on YouTube.

children.note: Texts 9 to 12 describe the functions of the mind. The verse counts ten senses plus false ego as the mind's eleven functions, with the sense objects, bodies, society and friendships as their fields of activity.
